Forensic Investigation team members examine the scene after two bike-borne suspects fired two rounds outside P.C. Jain Jewellers in Mahim on November 25, 2026 | Photo Credit: ANI
A firing incident targeting a jewellery store in Mumbai is suspected to be linked to a ₹10-crore extortion attempt after the shop owner received multiple threatening messages last month but chose to ignore them, police said, citing preliminary investigations.
One of the messages allegedly warned that even Z-Plus security cover won’t save the shop owner, police said on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
Also read | Police recover motorcycle allegedly used by accused in Mahim firing
Two motorcycle-borne individuals wearing helmets fired three rounds at the store of PC Jain Jewellers in Mahim on Wednesday (November 25) evening before fleeing towards Bandra. No one was hurt in the firing.
According to the police, the shop owner, Bharat Jain, had allegedly been receiving repeated threats through WhatsApp messages and phone calls over the past month. However, assuming the messages were spam, he ignored them and did not approach the police.
During the investigation, police found that Mr. Jain had received threatening communications on three separate occasions before the firing incident.
On October 18, Mr. Jain received a call from an unknown number. After he did not respond, a threatening message was sent to him in the evening, warning that he would be shot. On October 24, he received another message stating, “Ready rakhna, chamatkar hoga”.
The final threat, sent on October 31, reportedly included a direct demand for ₹10 crore along with a death threat, according to police.
The final message allegedly read: “Ramji, zyada dimaag mat chala, teri janam kundli hai. Z-Plus security bhi laga rakh, paisa tujhe dena hoga. Yamraj ji ko dekhna hai toh theek, nahi toh 10 crore dena hoga.”
The message warned Mr. Jain that even if he had Z-Plus security, one of the highest levels of protection provided to individuals facing severe or extreme threats, he would still have to pay the demanded amount or face fatal consequences.
Since the threats originated from unknown mobile numbers, the shop owner initially dismissed them as spam and did not lodge a police complaint.

Investigators suspect the firing was intended to intimidate Jain and pressure him into paying the ₹10 crore extortion amount.
Police said they are scanning CCTV footage from surrounding areas for clues to crack the case. Technical surveillance is also being used to identify and trace the two assailants who fled after the attack, they added.
